entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Current Replace-by-Fee (RBF) policy does not allow a transaction to be replaced simply by rebroadcasting it with the same fee, even if the fee-rate is relatively high. The existing mechanism mandates that any replacement transaction must include an absolute fee increase, which is determined in relation to the incrementalrelayfee parameter. This approach serves as a safeguard against denial-of-service (DoS) attacks by ensuring that spammers cannot continuously replace transactions without incurring additional costs.
Although there have been proposals to modify the default RBF policy, including suggestions like the one detailed at [this link](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/pipermail/bitcoin-dev/2018-February/015717.html), all known proposals have maintained the requirement for a minimal absolute fee increase as a protective measure. This ensures that the network remains robust and resistant to spam or malicious replacement activity, prioritizing security over mere convenience in transaction replacement.
